title: Acceptance-matrix line anchors rot silently: `#L<n>` is never checked against the test it was recorded for

labels.name: fr:in-progress
labels.description: An agent is actively working on this

body:
## Summary

Acceptance-matrix evidence refs carry line anchors (`super-fr:tests/unit/test_x.py#L542`). `fr acceptance check` verifies that the referenced **file** exists; nothing verifies that the **line** still lands on the test it was recorded for. Anchors rot whenever lines are added above them, silently, and the three committed reports then link readers to the wrong place — usually the middle of an unrelated test.

## It happened twice in one day, the second time to the author of the first finding

Both on 2026-09-21, both found by eye:

1. `run-unit-review-evidence` anchored `tests/integration/test_fr_goal_shape.py#L529`; the test had been at L542 since a format fix moved it. CI was green throughout. (Journal finding `f-stale-matrix-line-anchor`, #508 review.)
2. In #527 I added four rows, then applied review fixes that inserted lines into the same test files. Three of the eight anchors I had recorded *that afternoon* no longer pointed at a `def` — one landed on an `assert` in a different test. I only noticed because I happened to print the target lines while resolving an unrelated merge conflict.

The second is the instructive one: the person who had *just written a finding about this exact defect* reproduced it within hours. It is not a discipline problem.

## How widespread, measured

Scanned `main` at the time of filing: **58** `#L` anchors into `tests/**/*.py`; **57** land on a `def test_…`/`class Test…` line; **1** does not (`run-review-findings-gate` → `test_fr_goal_shape.py#L613`, a comment I anchored deliberately inside a long test — which is its own small argument that a line is the wrong unit).

So rot is *currently repaired*, not currently widespread — by hand, by luck. And that scan has a blind spot worth stating: it cannot see an anchor that slid onto a **different** test's `def`, which looks perfectly healthy.

## Mechanism

`fr.acceptance` treats a ref as `<repo>:<path>[#L<n>]` and resolves the path. The `#L<n>` fragment is carried through to the link renderers and never interpreted. A number is the most fragile possible pointer to a test: the thing it names (a function) has a stable identity, and the ref records its least stable property.

## Shape of a fix (not a recommendation)

Ordered by how much of the problem each removes:

- **Anchor on the name, render the line.** Record `path::test_name` (pytest's own node-id spelling), and let the report renderer resolve the current line at render time. The ref then cannot rot, and `fr acceptance check` can fail at authoring on a name that does not exist — a real check, where today there is none. Existing `#L` refs migrate mechanically wherever the line currently lands on a `def` (57 of 58 today).
- **Or a tripwire**, cheaper and weaker: every `#L<n>` into a test file must land on a `def test_`/`class Test` line. Catches rot the next time CI runs; does not prevent it, and shares the blind spot above.

The first moves the failure to authoring and makes the wrong state unrepresentable; the second only reports it sooner.

## Related

- **#522** — no verb can edit a row's `acceptance` text. Same family: the matrix records things it has no way to keep true. (Disclosure: #527 hand-edited two rows' acceptance text for exactly that reason, then regenerated the reports.)
- **#508 / #527** — where the instances above were found and repaired by hand.
- `.claude/rules/acceptance-matrix.md` — describes refs; says nothing about anchors.
